facts.statement: Fossils of Suuwassea were recovered during expeditions between 1999 and 2000 and formally described by Harris and Dodson in 2004.
facts.quote: The fossil remains were recovered in a series of expeditions during a period spanning the years 1999 and 2000 and were described by J.D. Harris and Peter Dodson in 2004.

facts.statement: Suuwassea lived during the Upper Jurassic in the Morrison Formation of southern Carbon County, Montana, USA.
facts.quote: Suuwassea is a genus of dicraeosaurid sauropod dinosaur found in Upper Jurassic strata of the Morrison Formation, located in southern Carbon County, Montana, United States.

facts.statement: Suuwassea is estimated to have been 15 meters long and weighed 5 metric tons.
facts.quote: Suuwassea is a dicraeosaurid, estimated to have reached 15 m in length and 5 MT in body mass

facts.statement: Suuwassea was a relatively small sauropod for its time, reaching 15 meters in length, 4 meters in height, and 5 tons in weight.
facts.quote: Fue un saurópodo de pequeño tamaño, comparado con los gigantes de su época, que alcanzó los 15 metros de largo, 4 de alto y 5 toneladas de peso.

facts.statement: The skull of Suuwassea possesses an enigmatic second hole, a feature not found in Diplodocus or its relatives which have only one hole near the nasal opening.
facts.quote: El cráneo presenta un enigmático segundo agujero, Diplodocus y sus parientes presentan solo uno relacionado con el orificio nasal.

facts.statement: Suuwassea's tail ended in short, flat vertebrae that gave it a whip-like shape.
facts.quote: La cola terminaba en vértebras cortas y planas, lo que le daba la forma de látigo.

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered by William Donawick, a veterinary professor at the University of Pennsylvania, who found a bone protruding from the ground while riding with his son-in-law.
facts.quote: El hallazgo lo realizó un profesor de veterinaria de la Universidad de Pensilvania, William Donawick, cuando cabalgaba con su yerno y se toparon con un hueso que sobresalía del suelo.

facts.statement: The fossil remains were in good condition, including preserved skull bones, having been partially exposed by erosion before excavation.
facts.quote: Los fósiles, que habían sido dejados parcialmente al descubierto por la erosión del terreno, se encontraban en buen estado, ya que incluso se conservaron los huesos del cráneo del animal.

facts.statement: The generic name Suuwassea is derived from the Crow Native American language term 'suuwassa', meaning 'the first thunder heard in spring', because the fossil was found in ancestral Crow territory.
facts.quote: Dado que el fósil fue encontrado en un territorio ancestral de la tribu de nativos americanos Crow, la etimología del nombre genérico se deriva de un término en su idioma, suuwassa, “el primer trueno que se escucha en primavera”.

facts.statement: The specific name 'emilieae' honors the late expedition sponsor Emilie deHellebranth.
facts.quote: El descriptor específico honra a la patrocinadora fallecida de las expediciones que recuperaron el fósil, Emilie deHellebranth.

facts.statement: In its original description, Suuwassea was classified as Flagellicaudata incertae sedis due to a mix of primitive and derived traits found in both dicraeosaurids and diplodocids.
facts.quote: In the original description, Suuwassea was placed at Flagellicaudata incertae sedis due to the mosaic of primitive and derived characters found in both dicraeosaurids and diplodocids.

facts.statement: Later studies reclassified Suuwassea as a North American member of the family Dicraeosauridae, though it was previously placed in the subfamily Apatosaurinae.
facts.quote: Later phylogenetic analysis placed it as a member of the diplodocid subfamily Apatosaurinae, but subsequent studies recovered it as a North American member of Dicraeosauridae.

facts.statement: Suuwassea is more closely related to dicraeosaurids, sharing the second postparital foramen with Dicraeosaurus, Tornieria, and Amargasaurus.
facts.quote: Aunque se halla más emparentado con los dicreosáuridos ya que el segundo foramen postparital se lo encuentra en Dicraeosaurus, Tornieria y Amargasaurus.

facts.statement: Suuwassea lived during the late Jurassic, approximately 147 million years ago in the Tithonian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 147 millones de años, en el Titoniense, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The discovery of Suuwassea coincides with other medium-sized sauropod finds in the northern Morrison Formation, contrasting with large animal finds in the southern sectors.
facts.quote: El hallazgo de S. emilieae es concurrente con otros hallazgos de saurópodos de tamaño mediano en la sección norte de la Formación Morrison contraria a los hallazgos de animales grandes en los sectores meridionales.

facts.statement: The presence of dicraeosaurid characters in a Laurasian diplodocoid raises open questions about the origin and distribution of ancestral diplodocooids.
facts.quote: La presencia de caracteres de dicreosáurido en un diplodocoide de Laurasia también planteaba la cuestión del origen y de la distribución de un diplodocoides ancestrales propuesta.

facts.statement: Suuwassea raises the debate of whether the group Flagellicaudata originated in Laurasia or Gondwana.
facts.quote: Suuwassea planteba preguntas si Flagellicaudata se originó en el Laurasia o en Gondwana.

facts.statement: It is debated whether dicraeosaurids existed before migrating from Laurasia, based on the primitive traits found in Suuwassea.
facts.quote: Esto podría también significar que había dicreosáuridos antes de la migración desde Laurasia.

facts.statement: Suuwassea lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (154.8 to 143.1 million years ago)
